notes: Read all 459 source lines before editing. This is non-visual, deterministic, side-effect-free utility code (source module JSDoc L1-9): the logic is ported VERBATIM. Every threshold, palette hex, numeric literal, ?? / != null fallback, Math/Map/Set/Date expression, regex, and sort comparator is byte-identical to the web original; only the two import lines (L10, L11) are remapped and prettier's native style (singleQuote, trailingComma 'all', arrowParens 'avoid') is applied. The web source is already semicolon-terminated so there is no semantic change.

Source L10 `import type { Drive } from '@/types/driving'` is remapped to `import type {Drive} from '../api/hooks/useDriving'` — the native location where the camelCase domain Drive type actually lives (useDriving.ts L57-84 is field-identical to web @/types/driving Drive: id/vehicleId/startTs/endTs/durationS/distanceM/startAddress/endAddress/.../startBatteryPct/endBatteryPct/avgSpeedMps/maxSpeedMps/...). Unit handling: source carries NO legacy Mi/Min/Mph/Kwh/Kw/Psi-suffixed fields — it reads SI-canonical Drive fields (distanceM metres, durationS seconds, maxSpeedMps m/s, startBatteryPct/endBatteryPct percent) and emits SI outputs (totalDistanceM, totalDurationS, topSpeedMps, avgEfficiencyWhKm). The one non-SI surface, PeriodStats.totalEnergyKwh / the cost-metric kWh accumulation, is an existing source field name reproduced verbatim (NOT a newly introduced suffix), so the SI-cutover guardrails are respected. No API paths and no i18n string literals exist in this source (the only string literals are grade labels, hex colours, the '::' pair separator, and YYYY-MM-DD regex/format) so there is nothing to translate; the display-boundary unit/locale conversion stays the caller's responsibility exactly as documented in the source JSDoc.

No DOM, window, document, Blob, URL, Recharts, Leaflet, react-leaflet, framer-motion, or old web-UI symbol reaches this native output; the sole runtime dependency is Intl.DateTimeFormat (via the inlined ymdInTz), which is Hermes-supported and already exercised in this native tree (lib/format.ts, web-parity/lib/currencyFormat.ts, and DrivesListPage.tsx's own inlined ymdInTz). There is therefore no browser-only behavior to gate and no 'unavailable' state to expose (contract rule 6 — faithful port of non-visual utility code). No co-located parity test was added, consistent with every other web-parity/lib parity port in this tree (numberFormat/currencyFormat/scoreScale/gpx).

Gates run from apps/native: `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit), `npm run lint -- --quiet` (eslint .), and `npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles` (jest) — all green; raw results in the final response.
